verdict.rationale: Stagehand is a code-first SDK for TypeScript, Python and Go. Its act/observe/extract primitives are composed in code, so multi-step flows can be scripted rather than issued as one-shot prompts. Its documented auto-caching turns agent-discovered workflows into deterministic scripts that can be re-run, and observe() lets code validate a step before acting on it. However, the evidence never explicitly documents loops, conditionals or parameterization as product features; these are implied only through the host language. missing for 10: explicit documentation of loop/conditional/parameterized workflow composition, independent hands-on corroboration of repeatable multi-step workflows.

support.subject: As an automation-engineer, I can compose repeatable multi-step workflows with loops, conditionals, and parameters instead of one-shot prompts

citations.quote: Use familiar APIs, self-healing actions, and network-level security across TypeScript, Python, and Go.
convert agent-discovered workflows into fast, deterministic scripts that run 10-100x faster
returns structured actions you can execute or validate before acting
